# `semicolon_separator`: `;` between expressions

March separates the expressions of a block with newlines; `;` is not part
of the language at all, so the lexer stops at it. The fix replaces the `;`
(and the blanks after it) with a line break at the current indentation, or
deletes a `;` that ends its line.

## A program that triggers it

```march
mod Main do
  needs IO.Console
  fn total() : Int do
    let x = 1; let y = 2
    x + y
  end

  fn main(_console : Cap(IO.Console)) do
    println(int_to_string(total()))
  end
end
```

## The fix

Put each expression on its own line.

```march
mod Main do
  needs IO.Console
  fn total() : Int do
    let x = 1
    let y = 2
    x + y
  end

  fn main(_console : Cap(IO.Console)) do
    println(int_to_string(total()))
  end
end
```

## Why the rule exists

Block structure comes from `do … end` and line breaks, so a block never
needs a terminator and the grammar has no sequencing operator. `;` is
caught in the lexer, at the character, because it would otherwise surface
as an unhelpful "unexpected character".

See also: [the language reference](https://github.com/march-language/march/blob/main/specs/lang/surface-syntax.md).
